Visva-Bharati begins digitising the manuscripts of its Lipika collection under Gyan Bharatam

The university in Santiniketan says work has started on thousands of rare manuscripts in Sanskrit, Bengali, Odia, Tamil and other languages, as part of the Ministry of Culture's national manuscript mission.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 12 November 2026

Where
Santiniketan, West Bengal

Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan has started digitising the manuscripts held at its Lipika Manuscriptorium (Lipika Puthisala), UNI and The Statesman reported on 4 November 2026. The collection holds thousands of rare manuscripts, along with archival documents and research materials.

According to The Statesman, the work began straight after the Puja holidays and covers texts in Sanskrit, Bengali, Odia and Tamil, among other languages. The information was shared by the university's spokesperson, Atig Ghosh, and by Professor Sisir Sahana, who is in charge of the manuscriptorium and is Principal of Kala Bhavana.

The project is part of Gyan Bharatam, the Ministry of Culture's nationwide mission to map, document and digitally archive India's manuscripts.

The reports do not say how long the work will take or when scans of the Lipika manuscripts will be open to readers.
